//: THE ONLY PLACE THE BOARD REPORT TAKES A NUMBER IT CANNOT COMPUTE ITSELF, and every entry names who measured it and when. The report reads GitHub for issues, the milestone and merges; those need no entry here. A gate result and the fleet-hours total cannot be read from GitHub, so they are recorded here VERBATIM by the agent that ran them. An absent or stale entry is printed as 'not reported since <date>' -- never omitted, and never estimated. The rule this enforces is the CEO's: nothing in the report comes from what an agent SAID, it comes from what merged and what gates PRINTED, so `output` must be the gate's own text and not a summary of it.

fleetHours.note: No cumulative total has been published. `fleet:hours` is built and measured (orchestrator, lead/fleet-hours) and reports 54.11 worker-hours across every capture on disk -- which spans several runs and protocol versions and is therefore NOT any single run's figure, which is why no edition carries it yet. Until an entry names one finished run, the report prints 'not instrumented' in those words.
fleetHours.//: A FLEET-HOURS ENTRY MUST NAME THE RUN IT WAS COMPUTED FROM **AND** THAT RUN'S finishedAt. The report REFUSES a total missing either, rather than printing it with a caveat -- a footnote is something a reader skips, and unlike a convention a refusal cannot be satisfied by remembering. `runFinishedAt` was added 2026-09-06 on orchestrator's suggestion after a total named a run still in flight: a NAMED but UNFINISHED run makes the field fillable and FALSE, which is harder to catch than a missing one. Shape (the placeholder values below are deliberately not plausible numbers -- an example that reads like data gets copied): {"total": "<HH h MM m, from the instrument, never typed>", "run": "<unit + InvocationID + case count + protocol>", "runFinishedAt": "<ISO 8601, the run's own finish, not when you recorded it>", "reportedBy": "orchestrator", "at": "<ISO 8601>", "method": "sum of each capture's last cumulative diagnostics.atMs -- never wall clock x worker count"}. Delete the `status` key when adding these. THE METHOD IS NOT NEGOTIABLE AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF IT WAS IMPOSSIBLE: this field read 'sum of per-case startedAt..finishedAt from the run's progress file' until orchestrator measured that no such data exists -- 0 of 1,623 cases carry any time field, because only the transient `current` array holds startedAt and an entry leaves it the moment the case completes. The timings a finished run needs are exactly the ones that file has discarded. Same shape as this repo's waiter polling for a `p.captured` that was never a field. The cost lives in each capture's own diagnostics, where bench-capture has read it all along. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES, so an edition can caveat it accurately: capture OCCUPANCY only -- not idle time between dispatches, not provisioning, reboots or power. It refuses rather than printing 0.00 when it billed nothing, and distinguishes 'no JSON found' from 'walked N and billed none'.

gates_//: Shape of a `gates` entry: {"command": "npm run lab:job -- -e job=rules-real-pages", "reportedBy": "orchestrator", "at": "<ISO 8601>", "output": "<the gate's OWN text, verbatim, not a summary>"}. The newest entry by `at` is the one printed. Older than `staleAfterHours` still prints, marked STALE and saying it describes an earlier state of the corpus -- an absent line and an old line mean different things and must never render the same.
